Vitamin K dietary requirements
The current Adequate Intakes (AI) for vitamin K in North America are set at 90 mg/d and 120 mg/d for women and men respectively,
19 years and older. The European Food Safety Administration (EFSA) recommends 70 mg/d for all adults 18 years old. These
recommendations are based on phylloquinone. In the US, current phylloquinone intakes approximate the AI, but the actual range
of intake is wide and varies across age groups, geographic regions, and racial/ethnic groups (Harshman et al., 2017). On average,
